Anna — quick technical summary ahead of the kickoff: 

1) Telemetry collected (Console + docs site):
- Console: auth events (user id hashes), API request/response metadata (endpoint, latency, status), usage metrics (tokens consumed, model id), and admin actions (role changes, key rotations). We do not log full prompt/response bodies in production by default unless a customer enables persistent logging for debugging.
- Docs site: standard web analytics (page views, referrer, browser user-agent).

2) Identifiers & PII/PHI:
- We collect user IDs as hashed identifiers for analytics by default. Email addresses and any PII/PHI must be explicitly stored per-customer; Redwood will not ingest PHI into hosted logs unless customer configures it. For customers that need PHI handling (HIPAA), we recommend Private or Dedicated and BAA contract.

3) Cookies & lifetimes:
- Console: session cookie (secure, SameSite=Lax, expires on session by default), persistent cookie for remember-me (30 days), CSRF token cookie (short-lived).
- Docs site (public): analytics cookie (third-party GA, 2 years default, configurable via cookie banner).

4) Logs & retention:
- Operational logs: 90 days by default in hosted, configurable for Dedicated/Private.
- Metrics/aggregates: 2 years.
- Per your request, we can provide a CSV data map showing event names, fields, retention, and PHI/PII flags (Telemetry-Data-Map.csv attached).

5) Encryption & access controls:
- All telemetry at rest is encrypted (AES-256). Access to raw logs is restricted to SRE/security roles and audited. We provide role-based access controls in the Console and support SSO (SAML/OIDC).

6) Next steps: I'll walk through the XLSX questionnaire items marked as technical during the kickoff. If there's anything you want me to pre-fill, point me to the tab names/rows and I'll prioritize those before the meeting.

Look forward to the call on 3/3.

- Dev
